items.followUp: State the modern periodic law and identify the quantity on which it is based.

rubric.why: The law describes the recurring periodic properties of elements.
rubric.description: States that the properties of elements are periodic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that elemental properties are periodic functions.

rubric.why: The periodicity in the modern periodic law is based on atomic number.
rubric.description: Identifies atomic number as the basis of the law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying atomic number.

modelAnswer: The properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

items.followUp: Explain how the electronegativity difference between two atoms affects the polarity of their bond.

rubric.why: Different electronegativities cause unequal attraction for shared electrons and make a bond polar.
rubric.description: Links an electronegativity difference to bond polarity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a difference in electronegativity makes the bond polar.

rubric.why: A greater electronegativity difference produces greater charge separation.
rubric.description: Explains how the size of the electronegativity difference affects polarity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a greater difference makes the bond more polar.

modelAnswer: A difference in electronegativity between bonded atoms makes the bond polar.
The greater the difference in electronegativity, the more polar the bond.

items.followUp: What is a triple covalent bond? Give one example.

rubric.why: A double covalent bond consists of two shared pairs of electrons.
rubric.description: Defines a double covalent bond in terms of shared electron pairs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that two pairs of electrons are shared between two atoms.

rubric.why: The example must contain a double covalent bond.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of a double covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an appropriate example, such as the oxygen molecule.

modelAnswer: A double covalent bond is formed when two pairs of electrons are shared between two atoms.

items.followUp: Why can evaporation take place even when a liquid is below its boiling point?

rubric.why: Evaporation takes place at the exposed surface of a liquid.
rubric.description: Identifies surface molecules as those that evaporate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning molecules at the liquid surface.

rubric.why: Some surface molecules have enough kinetic energy to escape into the air, so evaporation continues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that energetic surface molecules escape into the air.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is continuous because some molecules at the liquid surface always have sufficient kinetic energy to escape into the air.
It can therefore occur at any temperature, including below the boiling point.
